views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the Section 301 investigation on a tight, evidence-first track and use it—not a rushed global metals tariff—as the main lever on Beijing. Reopen talks aimed at written, verifiable commitments on forced tech transfer, JV/equity restrictions, discriminatory licensing, and cyber-enabled IP theft; treat the still-pending Section 232 menu as bargaining power, not an immediate global blast. Do not roll back the January Section 201 solar/washer safeguards, and do not offer purchase pledges or a tariff stand-down until China puts structural offers on the table.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is a modest opportunity, not a crisis. As of 1 March 2018 the dispute is still in the investigation/opening-salvo phase: the 14 Aug 2017 Section 301 memorandum launched an IP/tech-transfer case, the 8 Nov 2017 Beijing visit produced commercial MOUs but “no substantive concessions on structural IP / tech-transfer issues,” and the 22 Jan 2018 Section 201 action is a narrow safeguard (30% solar step-down; washer TRQs), not a China-wide tariff war. U.S. real-economy readings are not showing a trade-war bite: industrial production is still rising (INDPRO 101.71 in Feb), Michigan sentiment rebounded to 99.7, the funds rate is only 1.42%, and the yuan has strengthened (DEXCHUS 6.328 on 28 Feb), not cracked. The bilateral goods gap remains large (BOPGTB −74.6bn in Feb) and China’s IP and merchandise exports are firm, so Washington has room to press. That said, the opportunity is not −0.5-class: Commerce’s 16 Feb Section 232 options (24% global steel or 53% on 12 countries including China; 7.7% global aluminum or 23.6% on China/HK/Russia/Venezuela/Vietnam) are on the table but not due until April, DoD has already flagged ally-collateral risk, solar installers have warned of ~23k U.S. job losses from the 201 tariffs, China/Korea have already talked WTO challenges, and January commentary had USTR rumored to be considering very large 301 remedies before the statutory findings are even out. Escalating now—especially with a global 232 that hits Korea, the EU, and other partners—would convert unused leverage into a multi-front retaliation risk (farm and other U.S. exports) while the 301 legal record is still unfinished. Hence threat_score −0.30 and a slightly hawkish negotiate stance (action_score −0.10): hold the 201 line, finish 301, keep 232 targeted and unfired, and demand the structural IP terms Beijing refused in November.
key_factors: Section 301 is open but findings are not yet issued; Beijing Nov 2017 produced MOUs, not structural IP reform
Section 201 solar/washer safeguards are already in force and are the only live tariff action
Section 232 steel/aluminum menu published 16 Feb 2018; presidential decision not due until April; DoD prefers a targeted, China-focused option
U.S. macro is healthy (IP up, sentiment 99.7, no FX or growth shock); goods deficit with China remains large
Second-order risk: global 232 would hit allies and invite WTO/retaliation; domestic solar-installer job losses already alleged

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump signs memorandum directing USTR to investigate China's IP and technology-transfer practices under Section 301. USTR investigation initiated.
Trump visits Beijing; large package of commercial deals announced (many MOUs). No substantive concessions on structural IP / tech-transfer issues.
Trump approves Section 201 safeguard tariffs on solar panels and washing machines (China among suppliers hit). First major tariff action of the administration.
U.S. industrial production 101.7085 in Feb 2018, still rising over the window (+0.68).
Michigan consumer sentiment 99.7 in Feb 2018 after a January dip.
U.S. goods trade balance −74,571 million in Feb 2018, deficit wider by about $7.9bn over the window.
CNY per USD 6.328 on 28 Feb 2018, yuan stronger by ~3.2% over the window.
USTR initiated Section 301 on China tech transfer, IP, and innovation, covering JV/equity pressure, discriminatory licensing, directed acquisitions, and cyber-enabled theft.
Jan 2018: 301 findings officially due by August 2018, but reports that USTR may already be considering significant tariffs; China MOFCOM had expressed strong dissatisfaction at initiation.
22 Jan 2018: washer TRQs (20/18/16% then 50% over-quota) and solar safeguard 30% year 1 declining over four years; first 2.5 GW of cells excluded.
China and South Korea criticized the 201 action and suggested WTO complaints; White House advisers signaled steel/aluminum and other China measures could follow.

16 Feb 2018: Commerce recommends 24% global steel tariff or ≥53% on 12 countries including China, and 7.7% global aluminum or ~23.5% on China/HK/Russia/Venezuela/Vietnam; Trump must respond by mid-April.

DoD memo agrees some steel/aluminum imports impair security but prefers country-targeted options over global measures and flags harm to key allies; China said it would take necessary measures to protect its rights.
